references.text: When Joseph was elevated by Pharaoh, he received a ring on his hand and fine garments: "And Pharaoh took the signet ring from his own hand and put it on Joseph's hand, and clothed him in garments of fine linen" (Gen 41:42). The ring and the fine clothing symbolize honor and restoration, just as the father gives a ring and the best robe to the prodigal son.
Joseph gave his brothers change of clothes, expressing reconciliation and generosity (Gen 45:22). The parallel with the prodigal son is clear: the gifts of clothing mark reunion and forgiveness.

Isaiah describes being clothed in garments of salvation: "For he has clothed me with garments of salvation; he has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness" (Isa 61:10). The best robe that the father gives to his son can be seen as an image of God's righteousness clothing the repentant sinner.

In Zechariah, the high priest Joshua is clothed in new, clean garments after the filthy ones are removed, as a sign of forgiveness and restoration (Zech 3:4-5). This mirrors how the father clothes the returning son in the best robe.

Paul writes: "For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ" (Gal 3:27). Being clothed in new garments symbolizes the new identity one receives when returning to God, just as the son was clothed in the best robe.

Mordecai went out from the king in royal robes with a crown of gold and a mantle of fine linen and purple (Est 8:15). The ring and fine clothes are signs of honor and exaltation, just as the father honors the returning son.

In the Song of Songs there is an image of coming running with joy: "Listen! It is my beloved! See, he comes" (Song 2:8-9). The father's eagerness to receive his son and immediately clothe him in the best reflects deep love and longing.

The context for this verse: The father saw his son while he was still far off, was moved with compassion, ran to him, and embraced him (Luke 15:20). The gifts of clothes, a ring, and sandals in verse 22 are an immediate continuation of this loving reception.

Paul exhorts: "Put on the Lord Jesus Christ" (Rom 13:14). The image of being clothed in something new is central to the Christian understanding of repentance and renewal, just as the prodigal son was clothed in the finest robe.
The saved in Revelation are clothed in white robes (Rev 7:9). The best robe that the father gives to his son points forward to the final vindication and honor God gives to His children.
